text: Irakli Kupradze - The anti-Georgian “Dream” bringing the Defense Minister to the empty beach of Anaklia, where nothing is happening, for a photo session and a round of ministers walking in circles, is ridiculous propaganda that we will not believe! (07.05.2026, 13:56)

The anti-Georgian “Dream” bringing the Defense Minister yesterday to the empty beach of Anaklia, where no work is underway, for a photo session and the “Georgian Dream” minister’s round of walking around is ridiculous propaganda, which we, the citizens of Georgia, will not believe,” said the Secretary General of “Lelo-Strong Georgia,” Irakli Kupradze, at a briefing.
According to him, the Anaklia port was supposed to receive its first ship in 2020, but today we see a nonexistent project, failed negotiations, and Western investors driven out of the country.

“Anti-Georgian ‘Dream’ has gotten lost in its own lies. They are drowning in the propaganda and lies they produce. Yesterday, through the propaganda outlets of the anti-Georgian ‘Dream,’ reports were spread suggesting that the construction of the Anaklia port had supposedly begun. This is yet another bluff and trick by Bidzina Ivanishvili, indicating that the statements made by ‘Georgian Dream’ over the past 6 years were lies. For the umpteenth time—probably several dozen times—they announced that the construction of the Anaklia port had started today. In reality, everything is a lie, propaganda, and bluff on the part of Bidzina Ivanishvili.”

In 2024, under the conditions of yet another similar stunt, Bidzina Ivanishvili and his propaganda machine came out and said that within just a few days, an agreement would be signed with a Chinese consortium, which would also begin construction. Today, it is once again confirmed that all the promises made so far, all the dates, were lies. Only dry propaganda from Ivanishvili and the anti-Georgian “Dream.”

In 2026, today, there is no investor, nor a completed and built Anaklia port; there is no longer a master plan, a general plan that was supposed to have been agreed upon many times over. This general plan and master plan were both thrown into the trash. A new so-called master plan was ordered by the Ministry of Economy, according to which Ivanishvili and his anti-Georgian “Dream” are calling into question, in general, the purpose and effectiveness.

Yesterday, the anti-Georgian “Dream” bringing the Defense Minister to the empty beach of Anaklia, where no work is underway, for a photo op, and the “Georgian Dream” minister walking in circles is ridiculous propaganda that we, the citizens of Georgia, will not believe. One fact is clear: at a time when the Anaklia Port was supposed to receive its first ship in 2020, today we see a nonexistent project, failed negotiations, Western investors driven out of the country, American and European investors. Under these conditions, it is impossible for Ivanishvili to build the Anaklia Port. He does not want to build the Anaklia Port; he is interested in Georgia losing this most important strategic asset.

A new window of opportunities has clearly opened, which is reflected in our partners’ renewed and outspoken interest, showing that the Black Sea is of interest to our partners. Ivanishvili is depriving the country of this opportunity, and through propaganda he is trying to get by.

“Lelo Strong Georgia” is a political party that is the main supporter of this national and strategic project, the project called “Anaklia.” We have a specific plan for how the Anaklia project should be built. After coming to power, as the very first step, it must be declared that the Anaklia Port is a project of national and strategic importance; all contracts must be public, not behind a “black curtain,” as Ivanishvili does, whether it concerns “Arab cities” or anything else. The presence of Chinese and Russian investments that may contradict Georgia’s national interests must be deemed unacceptable. The Anaklia Port must be built with the involvement of the state, on the principle of cooperation with Western, American partners.
“No matter how many ministers walk along the Anaklia coast, where no work is underway, we will definitely build the port,” Kupradze notes.

We would like to remind you that yesterday, the Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development, Mariam Kvrivishvili, together with Vice Prime Minister and Minister of Defense Irakli Chikovani, inspected the ongoing works on the territory of the Anaklia port. As the Minister of Economy noted, “the process has already entered a fairly active phase.”
